episodes.request: How does the command line turn an evaluated value into text, and what does it do with strings and null? Just look, please, no changes.

steps.thought: The printing is probably in src/format.ts.

finish.report: formatValue in src/format.ts (line 15), called once from src/cli.ts line 57 as the last step of the eval command. A string is written with JSON.stringify, so it is in double quotes with its own quotes and control characters escaped; null is written as the word null; every other value, including numbers, booleans, lists, and objects, also goes through JSON.stringify, so a list prints as compact JSON such as [1,"a",null]. The result gets a line break from cli.ts. test/format.test.ts covers it with one test for quoting strings and writing lists, null, and a number.

episodes.request: What does the evaluator do for the in operator, and which errors can it raise? No changes.

steps.thought: List the error messages it raises.

finish.thought: The binary function holds the in case.
finish.report: In the binary function of src/evaluate.ts, the in operator first evaluates both sides. If the right side is a list, the result is true when some item equals the left value (compared through JSON text, so lists and objects compare by content). If both sides are strings, the result is whether the right string includes the left one. Anything else raises the EvalError '"in" needs a list or a string on its right'. Overall evaluate.ts raises nine EvalError sites with eight distinct messages: two numbers needed, unknown name, no field, only a list can be indexed by a whole number, index outside the list, minus needs a number, the in message, and division by zero (raised both for / and for %).
